title: Fixed covariance shrinkage before whitening
formal_object: Empirical train-only PSD covariance C, mu=tr(C)/d>0, alpha in (0,1], ridge rho>0; C_alpha=(1-alpha)C+alpha mu I+rho I.
assumptions: Covariance is centered on training inputs; evaluate with the same fixed means/maps.
The shared diagonal shift bounds inverse amplification; it need not improve downstream ranking.
Fixed alpha=.2 is not an estimated Ledoit-Wolf or OAS optimum.

operations.output: Shrink toward isotropy before inverse-root whitening.

derivation_steps.justification: Identity commutes with C, so the common eigenbasis gives an exact spectral formula.
C eigenvalues are nonnegative; the minimum sets the inverse-root operator norm.
Increasing the diagonal shift controls anisotropy but changes useful directions; this is an amplification statement, not a retrieval excess-risk theorem.

method_expression: Compute train-only means and fixed-alpha covariance inverse root with recorded actual eigenvalue floor; transform both sides and output complete dot-product rankings. Match the existing ridge in every control.
distinguishing_prediction: Unstable small empirical eigenvalues cause less amplification under shrinkage; any useful benefit must survive comparison with ordinary ridge and fitted covariance shrinkage.
falsifier: Same-ridge whitening, diagonal scaling, OAS or Ledoit-Wolf gives the same or better native tradeoff, or shrinkage removes informative rare directions.
closest_alternative: Ridge whitening, Ledoit-Wolf and OAS. Fixed alpha changes the metric but contributes no new covariance estimator theorem.
decisive_comparison: Same train data/PCA/means/ridge and native candidates; retain spectral diagnostics plus full per-task outcomes and complete costs.
legacy_code_audit: Legacy invsqrt also floors eigenvalues; because C_alpha already includes ridge its floor is redundant in exact arithmetic. C_WHITEN is already regularized.
review_limit: Amplification identity reviewed; optimal-estimator and accuracy claims withheld.
